results.title: Frontiers | Turn-timing in signed conversations: coordinating stroke-to-stroke turn boundaries
results.content: # Turn-timing in signed conversations: coordinating stroke-to-stroke turn boundaries. Cross-linguistic comparison has indicated that spoken languages vary only minimally in terms of turn-timing, and language acquisition research has shown pre-linguistic vocal turn-taking in the first half year of life. To address this question we look at turn-timing in question–answer sequences in spontaneous conversations of Sign Language of the Netherlands. The findings indicate that although there is considerable overlap in two or more signers’ articulators in conversation, when proper allowance is made for onset preparation, post-utterance retraction and the intentional holding of signs for response, turn-taking latencies in sign look remarkably like those reported for spoken language. A leading question for the research reported here is to what extent sign language users also operate the same turn-taking system as used in spoken languages, especially with regard to turn-timing. If this were the case, turn-timing in signed interactions as calculated by stroke-to-stroke turn boundaries should be within the same cross-linguistic range as has previously been reported for spoken languages.

results.content: # How Blurred Boundaries Lead to Ambiguous Relationships. ## Opposite-Sex Friendships: When “Maybe More Than Friends” Starts — It’s Usually When These 3 Lines Get Blurred. A few years back, the word “maybe more than friends” became super popular. It’s about how guys and girls interact. If they don’t know where to draw the line, they can easily end up in a “maybe more than friends” situation. Some say it’s “more than just friends, but not quite dating.” Others say it’s “acting like a couple while still calling each other friends.”. Everyone has their own opinion on what it means. But when guys and girls start getting close, it almost always starts when they let these lines get blurry:. ## The “Deep Secrets” Line. The world is big, but people’s hearts can feel big or small. Sometimes, life gets you down, and you end up with a lot on your mind. It can feel like too much to handle alone, so you need to talk to someone. If guys and girls don’t have boundaries when they’re sharing their feelings, or if they lower those boundaries, things can get complicated. ## Written by PhoebeWhite.
